☂️ Good Friday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 567 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Carolyn DiPaolo for copy editing.

 
 
1 big thing: Stormy weekend ahead
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

A powerful nor'easter is expected to drench the Northeast U.S. this weekend, while Hawaii braces for the potentially life-threatening effects of Hurricane Nolo.

  • In a rare rhyming tropical duet in the Pacific, Hurricane Nolo is nearing Hawaii while Hurricane Polo threatens Mexico's coast.

⛈️ Coastal New Jersey, New York and New England could be particularly hard-hit by the slow-moving and long-lasting nor'easter.

  • Rainfall totals will depend on the storm's track, but officials throughout the area are preparing for the worst.

💨 Strong winds and coastal flooding are major threats as well.

  • Power outages are possible. The storm could also snarl operations at key airports in the area, including JFK, LaGuardia, Newark and Boston Logan.
  • Airlines are already offering free flight changes.

🌀 Meanwhile, the National Hurricane Center is warning of possible "catastrophic and life-threatening flooding" on Hawaii's Big Island tied to Hurricane Nolo.

  • Nolo's center is expected to stay offshore. But forecasters are still warning of 10-15 inches of rain for some parts of the Big Island, with the potential for up to 25.
  • It's forecast to become a major hurricane by tomorrow afternoon.

The NHC says: "This rainfall could produce catastrophic life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain."

  • Storm surge is also a major risk, especially if Nolo lines up with high tide.

Nor'easter forecast ... Hurricane Nolo forecast.
 
 
2. 🏛️ GOP House danger deepens
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

House Republicans are on track to lose their majority during the midterms, Axios' Kate Santaliz reports from a new forecast.

  • Cook Political Report shifted 15 House races toward Democrats today — the latest sign that the political environment is deteriorating for Republicans.

🪑 Democrats only need a net gain of three seats to take the majority.

  • Cook now projects that Democrats are most likely to gain between five and 15 seats, which would give them a 220-230-seat majority.

🖼️ The big picture: Republicans have been arguing that redistricting and a sizable financial advantage give them more breathing room.

  • But Cook says new Democratic maps in California and Utah are largely offsetting Republicans' redistricting gains elsewhere.

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
From left: Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan, Chinese President Xi Jinping, President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump leave the National Archives Museum after a tour today. Photo: Win McNamee/Getty Images
  1. 🇨🇳 President Trump asked Chinese President Xi Jinping to halt any assistance to Iran when the two spoke during his state visit, U.S. Ambassador to Beijing David Perdue said today. More from Barak Ravid.
  2. 🗳️ The Supreme Court is letting the Trump administration use a modified program to verify voters' citizenship status for now, handing the administration a last-minute win in its campaign for new election rules ahead of the midterms. Go deeper.
  3. 🤖 Pope Leo XIV warned today that a "paradise of machines" risked undermining humanity, as he opened a trip to France by posing fundamental questions about what it means to be human in the AI age. Go deeper.
 
 
4. ❤️ 1 song thing: Nashville celebrates Dolly Day
 
Dolly Parton performs in Nashville in 2025. Photo: Jason Kempin/Getty Images

Music City is going all out to celebrate Dolly Day, Axios Nashville's Adam Tamburin reports.

  • The celebration falls on 9/25, paying homage to Dolly Parton's classic "9 to 5."

🎉 More than 145 events, parties and fundraisers are planned across the city.

  • Coffee shops and bars are launching Dolly-themed menu items, many of them featuring her signature shades of pink.

🎸 Local music venues will host performances of "9 to 5" at 5 p.m.

  • A downtown fireworks show at 9:25 p.m. will cap the celebration.
